text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The armed forces tomorrow begin their biggest strategic manoeuvres ever, covering the zones of all the field army corps and including all branches of the armed forces. Known as Badr 96, they will last 10 days.

- Egypt has asked Israel to go back on attitudes which threaten the peace process. A diplomatic source said: "The atmosphere of tension which Israel is spreading opens the door to violence in the region."

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said the aim of the London conference was to plan to overthrow Arab governments. He said those who would have taken part are working for foreign governments and receive massive financing. He said that the British government responded to contacts from Egypt and other countries and prevented the conference taking place.

- The State Security Investigation Department released the photos of six men wanted for "terrorist" offences and appealed to the public to come forward with any information on their whereabouts. The pictures are of Ahmed Yahya, Adel Yahya, Yahya Yahya, Taha Yahya, Hussein Fayed and Abdelnaby Ahmed Ali.
- The Minister of Public Works and Water Resources, Abdel-Hadi Radi, fainted at Cairo airport just before he was due to fly to Paris for medical treatment. He was taken to hospital but is now stable.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the government was committed to respecting the constitutional court's ruling that a stamp duty on capital was unconstitutional. The government is working out how much it will cost to abolish it.
- Egypt informs Turkey that it cannot accept encroachment on Iraqi sovereignty and that there can be no justification for setting up a buffer zone.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said the police have arrested 94 percent of those who committed recent acts of terrorism and security in Egypt is among the best in the world.
- The level of the water in Lake Nasser has risen to 176.15 metres above sea level and the Ministry of Public Works is preparing for the autumn flood season.
- Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi, on eve of big military manoeuvres, says "We are ready for all possibilities."

- President Hosni Mubarak, in remarks to Mayo newspaper, says Egypt is against partitioning Iraq because it would be a danger to the whole region. He said that the fruits of economic reform are many and varied.
- The offer of shares in Telemisr was 10 times oversubscribed. The way the shares will be allocated is still under discussion.
